title: Nine Moves of Learning
subtitle: 棋类与对弈 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 棋类与对弈（文学艺术与体育·棋牌与竞技）
meta: 主题语境：棋类与对弈（文学艺术与体育·棋牌与竞技）　|　核心词汇：chess　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 chess 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 my mother was sent to learn ① chess she could not win, and she said the learning was the whole of the lesson. The ② chess, meaning the game and not the board, was nine moves long and was learned by whoever came last; chess, she said, is the only thing in a club that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ chess in that club had the same opening, and the ④ chess at the end, meaning the one the master kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever learned properly. Chess, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ chess was the whole of the afternoon, meaning the contest it carried and not the game. The ⑥ chess, meaning the contest and not any of that, is the only thing in an afternoon that everybody watches and nobody questions; chess, he said, is either something you learn or the only word that means both a game and a contest. She said the contest is the part they remember.

By 1961 the ⑦ chess had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the opening. The ⑧ chess of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine moves and eleven years of learning; chess, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ chess I remember is the one at the end, which was learned in 1966 and is still described as the slowest in the county. A ⑩ chess, my grandmother said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being learned; every chess, she said, is a contest that has agreed to look like a game. She said the contest was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 棋局（指那一局棋本身，与那块棋盘相对）
C. 固定搭配：learn chess 学下棋
D. n. 棋局（指那个俱乐部里每一局）
E. n. 棋局（指末尾那一局）
F. n. 对弈（抽象：它承载的那场较量）
G. n. 那场较量（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The chess, meaning the game and not the board
chess was the whole of the afternoon
the chess had become a number in a report
The chess of the whole thing
A chess, my grandmother said in 1971

answers.why: learn chess 意为“学下棋”，1946 年母亲被派去学她赢不了的那门棋。
chess 意为“国际象棋”，指那一局棋本身而不是那块棋盘，共九步，由最后来的人学会。
chess 指那个俱乐部里每一局棋，每一局都是同样的开局。
chess 指末尾那一局（棋手保留的那一局），是唯一有人认真学过的。
chess 意为“对弈”，抽象指它承载的那场较量，父亲说 chess 就是那个下午的全部。
chess 为抽象用法，指那场较量本身，是一个下午里人人都看、却没人质疑的东西。
chess 意为“国际象棋”，到 1961 年这局 chess 成了报告里的一个数字。
chess 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九步和十一年的学习。
chess 意为“棋局”，我记得的是末尾那一局，1966 年学过，至今仍被说成全县最慢的。
chess 为抽象总称，祖母说一局棋是唯一会因为被认真学习而变好的东西。
